title: Hom on further slices and bidual pullback compatibility
statement: Fix a prime l, a normalized base comparison family [lem-sf-adic-module-section-data], coefficient ring isomorphisms c on all site objects and normalized module restriction data [lem-sf-adic-slice-restriction]. Two equations hold: the base internal-Hom comparisons on every further slice commute with the actual adicUpperStarIhomIso and the normalized restriction section map; and the base bidual maps commute with actual native pullback through adicComparisonDualSlice and the contravariant Mod.ihomMap. The precise equations are the hom_slice and bidual_slice fields of AdicSliceClosedData. This assertion contains no coefficient or module restriction construction, tensor comparison or evaluation restriction assertion, and does not claim biduality is invertible.

source.place: Sections Localization of ringed sites, Tensor product and Internal Hom; definition-localize-ringed-site, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, lemma-internal-hom-restriction and lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor. Specialization and normalization steps of lem-sf-adic-module-slice-compatibility; the native constructions in lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Mod/Evaluation.lean and lean/WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/ProEtale/Adic/InternalHomEvaluation.lean.

proof.text: For any supplied base comparison P, evaluate naturality of its homIso along W.hom.op and use section_restriction. The definition of the sectionwise internal Hom restricts a slice morphism by Over.map; evaluation at the identity object of the further slice therefore identifies its value at W with P.sectionsEquiv applied to native evaluation of the restricted Hom section. This is the private hom_sections lemma, using the actual homObj of [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and the supplied evaluation field of [lem-sf-adic-module-section-data].

The native upperStarIsoSheafPushforward is monoidal. Its tensor coherence, naturality of Sheaf.tensorObjComparison and the proved pushforward tensor formula identify the pullback tensorator on pure tensors with literal restriction. Compose the existing adicUpperStarIhomIso_evaluation with this localization isomorphism. Naturality of localization and evaluation on a pure tensor give evaluation_restriction, without a tensor comparison assumption or an additional theorem with sorry. These are existing native APIs imported by [lem-sf-adic-module-section-data].

Apply hom_sections to both sides of hom_slice, then use slice_sections from [lem-sf-adic-slice-restriction]. Naturality of the native Hom comparison moves W.hom.op across that comparison. Apply evaluation_restriction on W.left and naturality of the localization isomorphism. Applying the base additive section equivalence to this equality gives the required hom_slice equation on every further object.

First combine native evaluation compatibility with evaluation_naturality for the actual adicUpperStarUnitIso to obtain dual_evaluation. For bidual_slice apply Mod.hom_ext_of_evaluation, the existing counit-injectivity principle of [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint], to the underlying maps. The left transpose becomes the pullback of the supplied base bidual_transpose by tensorator naturality and dual_evaluation. Lax braidedness moves the braiding through pullback. On the right, evaluation_ihomMap moves the dual comparison to the argument; whisker exchange and the supplied local bidual_transpose identify the result with the same braided evaluation by braiding naturality. No bidual invertibility is used. Pair this equation with hom_slice to construct AdicSliceClosedData.

theorem adicSliceClosedCompatibility (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (base : ∀ X : Scheme.{u}, AdicModuleSectionComparison l X)
    (c : ∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.ProEt),
      (base U.left).ring ≅
        (localizationRestriction RingCat.{u + 1} U.hom U.prop).obj (base X).ring)
    (r : AdicSliceRestrictionData l base c) :
    AdicSliceClosedData l base c r
